children: Greece-based petroleum and drybulk shipper's Q2 revenue rose nearly 140% yr/yr on fleet growth, higher rates
Adjusted net income and adjusted EPS more than doubled from a year earlier
Company reported strong cash position and remains debt free
Company expects fleet to grow to 25 vessels with scheduled deliveries in 2026
Imperial Petroleum says it is well equipped to navigate shifting geopolitical landscapes
FLEET EXPANSION - Co said revenue growth was primarily due to a 6.9 vessel increase in the average number of vessels in its fleet
HIGHER SHIPPING RATES - Co cited increased tanker and drybulk rates, driven by geopolitical tensions and favorable drybulk market dynamics
INCREASED SPOT ACTIVITY - Co said higher voyage expenses were mainly due to a 58.4% increase in spot days and increased bunker prices
The one available analyst rating on the shares is "buy"
The average consensus recommendation for the renewable fuels peer group is "buy"
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for Imperial Petroleum Inc is $9.00, about 67.9% above its September 9 closing price of $5.36
The stock recently traded at 2 times the next 12-month earnings vs. a P/E of 2 three months ago
